overall: The AG found the County Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by not taking roll call votes during remote-participation meetings and by using a secret ballot, both cured by later action; no deliberation violation was found, and no further relief was ordered.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the County Commission did not take votes by roll call at its February 25 meeting although several commissioners participated remotely.
allegations.key_passage: During the County Commission's February 25 and March 11 meetings, two County Commissioners participated remotely, however votes taken during these meetings were not by roll call.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the County Commission voted by secret ballot to appoint Airport Commission members at its March 11 meeting, using written ballots.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law explicitly prohibits votes taken by secret ballot.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that commissioners must have deliberated on Airport Commission appointments outside a meeting, given the lack of discussion at the March 11 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: In the absence of evidence to the contrary, we credit the County Commission members' statements and find that they did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Amend the minutes of the February 25 and March 11 meetings to indicate that the remedial roll call votes were taken during a subsequent meeting and to describe the results of those subsequent votes.
remedy_passage: The County Commission should also amend the minutes from the February 25 and March 11 meetings to indicate that such remedial action was taken during a subsequent meeting and to describe the results of the subsequent votes.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
